explain: With AWS Systems Manager Session Manager, you can manage your Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instances, edge devices, on-premises servers, and virtual machines (VMs). You can use either an interactive one-click browser-based shell or the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI). It provides secure and auditable node management without the need to open inbound ports, maintain bastion hosts, or manage SSH keys.

q: A company uses Amazon API Gateway to manage its REST APIs that third-party service providers access. The company must protect the REST APIs from SQL injection and cross-site scripting attacks. What is the MOST operationally efficient solution that meets these requirements?

o.t: Configure AWS WAF.
o.w: AWS WAF can be associated directly with an API Gateway REST API, letting the company apply managed rule groups for SQL injection and cross-site scripting protection without introducing any additional service layer.

o.t: Set up API Gateway with an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Configure AWS WAF in CloudFront.
o.w: Adding a CloudFront distribution in front of API Gateway just to attach WAF introduces an unnecessary extra component and cost when WAF can already be associated with API Gateway directly.

o.t: Configure AWS Shield.
o.w: AWS Shield protects against DDoS attacks at the network and transport layers; it does not inspect HTTP request content and therefore cannot detect or block SQL injection or cross-site scripting payloads.

o.t: Set up API Gateway with an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Configure AWS Shield in CloudFront.
o.w: This combines the unnecessary CloudFront layer with Shield, which, as with the WAF-less Shield option, does not address content-based attacks like SQL injection or XSS at all.

explain: AWS WAF (Web Application Firewall) is specifically designed to protect web applications from common web exploits like SQL injection and cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks. By configuring AWS WAF with API Gateway, you can create rules to filter and allow or block requests based on defined conditions, providing protection against various types of attacks.

q: A company has hired an external vendor to perform work in the company’s AWS account. The vendor uses an automated tool that is hosted in an AWS account that the vendor owns. The vendor does not have IAM access to the company’s AWS account. How should a solutions architect grant this access to the vendor?

o.t: Create an IAM user in the company’s account with a password that meets the password complexity requirements. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the user for the permissions that the vendor requires.
o.w: Creating a long-lived IAM user with a password in the company's account means distributing and managing durable credentials to an external party, which is less secure than temporary, assumable role-based access.

o.t: Create a new identity provider by choosing “AWS account” as the provider type in the IAM console. Supply the vendor’s AWS account ID and user name. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the new provider for the permissions that the vendor requires.
o.w: IAM does not offer an 'AWS account' identity provider type for configuring this kind of cross-account access; cross-account access is granted through IAM roles and trust policies, not an identity-provider construct.

o.t: Create an IAM role in the company’s account to delegate access to the vendor’s IAM role. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the role for the permissions that the vendor requires.
o.w: Creating an IAM role with a trust policy that allows the vendor's IAM role to assume it lets the vendor obtain short-lived, temporary credentials scoped to only the permissions attached to the role, the standard and secure cross-account access pattern with no shared long-term credentials.

o.t: Create an IAM group in the company’s account. Add the tool’s IAM user from the vendor account to the group. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the group for the permissions that the vendor requires.
o.w: IAM users and their credentials belong to the account that created them; you cannot add another AWS account's IAM user directly into your own account's IAM group, so this is not a valid mechanism for cross-account delegation.

explain:
IAM roles allow you to delegate access to resources in your AWS account to another AWS account. In this case, you can create a role in your account and grant the vendor's IAM role permission to assume that role.

By doing this, the vendor can use temporary security credentials obtained by assuming the role to access resources in your account. This ensures that the vendor doesn't need IAM credentials from your account.

q: A company runs a website that stores images of historical events. Website users need the ability to search and view images based on the year that the event in the image occurred. On average, users request each image only once or twice a year. The company wants a highly available solution to store and deliver the images to users. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.t: Store images in Amazon S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA). Use S3 Standard-IA to directly deliver images by using a static website.
o.w: S3 Standard-IA charges a per-GB data retrieval fee every time an image is served, and across a large catalog of images this recurring, if infrequent, access can accumulate retrieval costs that offset the lower storage price, making total cost less predictable than Standard.

o.t: Store images in Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS). Use a web server that runs on Amazon EC2.
o.w: Running a web server on EC2 to serve files from EFS requires provisioning, patching, and scaling a server fleet, introducing ongoing compute costs that a static-website-enabled S3 bucket avoids entirely.

o.t: Store images in Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS). Use a web server that runs on Amazon EC2.
o.w: EBS volumes attach to a single EC2 instance and are not natively highly available across multiple Availability Zones without additional replication, and this option still requires managing EC2 web servers, both of which add cost and complexity.

o.t: Store images in Amazon S3 Standard. Use S3 Standard to directly deliver images by using a static website.
o.w: S3 Standard is already durable and available across multiple Availability Zones, has no retrieval fees, and can serve the images directly through static website hosting, giving a simple, serverless, highly available solution without the extra retrieval charges or server management the other options require.

q: A company wants to analyze and troubleshoot Access Denied errors and Unauthorized errors that are related to IAM permissions. The company has AWS CloudTrail turned on. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST effort?

o.t: Search CloudTrail logs with Amazon Athena queries to identify the errors.
o.w: Athena can query CloudTrail logs stored in S3 directly with standard SQL, letting the company search for specific error codes such as AccessDenied or UnauthorizedOperation with no infrastructure to provision.

o.t: Use AWS Glue and write custom scripts to query CloudTrail logs for the errors.
o.w: Writing and maintaining custom AWS Glue ETL scripts just to parse and query CloudTrail logs requires significantly more development and operational effort than querying the logs directly with Athena.

o.t: Search CloudTrail logs with Amazon QuickSight. Create a dashboard to identify the errors.
o.w: QuickSight is a business intelligence visualization tool; before building a dashboard with it, the company would still need a queryable data source such as Athena underneath, making this effectively a bigger lift for a one-off troubleshooting search.

o.t: Use AWS Batch and write custom scripts to query CloudTrail logs for the errors.
o.w: AWS Batch is designed for running batch computing jobs, not SQL-style log querying, and would require custom scripting to parse and search CloudTrail logs, well beyond the least-effort requirement.

explain:
Amazon Athena allows you to query data directly from S3 using standard SQL queries.
CloudTrail logs can be stored in Amazon S3, and Athena makes it easy to analyze the logs using SQL queries.

q: A company runs an internal browser-based application. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The instances run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. The Auto Scaling group scales up to 20 instances during work hours, but scales down to 2 instances overnight. Staff are complaining that the application is very slow when the day begins, although it runs well by mid-morning. How should the scaling be changed to address the staff complaints and keep costs to a minimum?

o.t: Implement a target tracking action triggered at a lower CPU threshold, and decrease the cooldown period.
o.w: Lowering the target CPU threshold and shortening the cooldown period makes the Auto Scaling group react and add capacity sooner as load ramps up in the morning, without maintaining unnecessary capacity overnight, minimizing cost while fixing the slow start.

o.t: Implement a scheduled action that sets the desired capacity to 20 shortly before the office opens.
o.w: Setting desired capacity to 20 shortly before the office opens provisions the maximum fleet size every single morning regardless of that day's actual demand, running at peak cost even on lighter-traffic days.

o.t: Implement a scheduled action that sets the minimum and maximum capacity to 20 shortly before the office opens.
o.w: Raising the minimum and maximum capacity to 20 keeps 20 instances running at all times once set, removing the ability to scale back down later and driving costs far higher than necessary rather than keeping costs to a minimum.

o.t: Implement a step scaling action triggered at a lower CPU threshold, and decrease the cooldown period.
o.w: Step scaling with a lower threshold could help responsiveness, but target tracking's continuous metric-following approach more smoothly and automatically maintains the target CPU without the extra step-size tuning that step scaling requires.

q: A company recently created a disaster recovery site in a different AWS Region. The company needs to transfer large amounts of data back and forth between NFS file systems in the two Regions on a periodic basis. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.t: Set up an SFTP server on Amazon EC2.
o.w: Standing up and maintaining a self-managed SFTP server on EC2 for recurring transfers requires ongoing patching, scaling, and scripting, far more operational overhead than a managed transfer service.

o.t: Use AWS Snowball devices.
o.w: Snowball is designed for one-time or infrequent bulk, offline transfers using physical devices, which is a poor fit for data that needs to move periodically between two live, active file systems.

o.t: Use AWS DataSync.
o.w: AWS DataSync is purpose-built to move data efficiently between NFS file systems on a recurring schedule, with built-in scheduling, retries, and verification, requiring minimal operational effort for periodic transfers.

o.t: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS).
o.w: AWS DMS is designed for migrating and replicating relational or certain NoSQL database engines, not generic NFS file data, so it is not the appropriate tool for this file-transfer use case.

explain: If we want to transfer large amount of data we can used AWS Datasync.

q: A company hosts an online shopping application that stores all orders in an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Single-AZ DB instance. Management wants to eliminate single points of failure and has asked a solutions architect to recommend an approach to minimize database downtime without requiring any changes to the application code. Which solution meets these requirements?

o.t: Convert the existing database instance to a Multi-AZ deployment by modifying the database instance and specifying the Multi-AZ option.
o.w: Modifying the existing instance to enable the Multi-AZ option creates a synchronously replicated standby in another Availability Zone with automatic failover, directly eliminating the single point of failure with no application changes.

o.t: Create a read-only replica of the PostgreSQL database in another Availability Zone. Use Amazon Route 53 weighted record sets to distribute requests across the databases.
o.w: A read-only replica provides no automatic failover for write traffic, and routing requests via Route 53 weighted records to split reads and writes would require application changes, violating the no-code-changes requirement.

o.t: Create a new RDS Multi-AZ deployment. Take a snapshot of the current RDS instance and restore the new Multi-AZ deployment with the snapshot.
o.w: Creating a brand-new Multi-AZ deployment from a snapshot means provisioning an entirely new database instance with a new endpoint and cutting over, which is more complex and causes more downtime than simply enabling Multi-AZ on the existing instance.

o.t: Place the RDS for PostgreSQL database in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group with a minimum group size of two. Use Amazon Route 53 weighted record sets to distribute requests across instances.
o.w: Running a relational database inside an EC2 Auto Scaling group with Route 53 weighted routing is not how RDS high availability works and would require substantial custom engineering for data synchronization and failover, well beyond a simple Multi-AZ toggle.

explain: By converting the existing RDS instance to a Multi-AZ deployment, you enable high availability with automatic failover. Amazon RDS will automatically replicate the database to a standby instance in a different Availability Zone (AZ). In the event of a failure, Amazon RDS will automatically promote the standby to the primary, minimizing downtime.

q: A solutions architect wants all new users to have specific complexity requirements and mandatory rotation periods for IAM user passwords. What should the solutions architect do to accomplish this?

o.t: Use third-party vendor software to set password requirements.
o.w: Using third-party software to manage IAM password requirements adds unnecessary cost and complexity when IAM already provides this capability natively.

o.t: Attach an Amazon CloudWatch rule to the Create_newuser event to set the password with the appropriate requirements.
o.w: CloudWatch has no native trigger tied to a 'Create_newuser' IAM event for enforcing password requirements, and even a custom workaround would just be reimplementing something IAM already handles centrally.

o.t: Set an overall password policy for the entire AWS account.
o.w: IAM lets the company configure a single account-wide password policy that enforces complexity requirements and rotation periods for all IAM users automatically, exactly matching the requirement with minimal configuration.

o.t: Set a password policy for each IAM user in the AWS account.
o.w: IAM password policies apply at the account level, not per individual user; there is no IAM mechanism to set a distinct password policy for each separate user, so this approach does not reflect how IAM actually works.

explain: Amazon Web Services (AWS) allows you to set an account-wide password policy using AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM). This policy defines the rules and requirements for all IAM users in the AWS account. It's a centralized approach to enforce security measures consistently across all users. In this case, the solutions architect can set the specific complexity requirements and mandatory rotation periods by configuring the password policy at the AWS account level.

q: A recent analysis of a company's IT expenses highlights the need to reduce backup costs. The company's chief information officer wants to simplify the on-premises backup infrastructure and reduce costs by eliminating the use of physical backup tapes. The company must preserve the existing investment in the on-premises backup applications and workflows. What should a solutions architect recommend?

o.t: Set up AWS Storage Gateway to connect with the backup applications using the NFS interface.
o.w: An NFS-based Storage Gateway (file gateway) presents a file share, not a tape-emulation interface, so the existing tape-based backup software could not use it without reconfiguring how it writes backups.

o.t: Set up an Amazon EFS file system that connects with the backup applications using the NFS interface.
o.w: Amazon EFS is a file system, not a virtual tape library, and connecting over NFS still requires reconfiguring the backup application away from its existing tape-based workflow, so it does not preserve the current investment.

o.t: Set up AWS Storage Gateway to connect with the backup applications using the iSCSI-virtual tape library (VTL) interface.
o.w: AWS Storage Gateway's Tape Gateway presents an iSCSI-virtual tape library interface that emulates physical tape drives and media changers, letting the existing backup software keep operating exactly as it does today while virtual tapes are stored durably in Amazon S3 and Glacier, eliminating physical tapes with no workflow changes.

o.t: Set up an Amazon EFS file system that connects with the backup applications using the iSCSI interface.
o.w: Amazon EFS does not expose an iSCSI interface at all; EFS is only accessible over NFS, so this option describes a capability EFS does not actually have.

explain:
AWS Storage Gateway provides a hybrid cloud storage service that enables on-premises applications to seamlessly use cloud storage.
The iSCSI-virtual tape library (VTL) interface of AWS Storage Gateway is designed to integrate with existing backup applications that use tape-based workflows. It emulates a tape library, allowing you to store virtual tapes in Amazon S3 or Glacier, providing a cost-effective and scalable alternative to physical tapes.

q: A company is running an SMB file server in its data center. The file server stores large files that are accessed frequently for the first few days after the files are created. After 7 days the files are rarely accessed. The total data size is increasing and is close to the company's total storage capacity. A solutions architect must increase the company's available storage space without losing low-latency access to the most recently accessed files. The solutions architect must also provide file lifecycle management to avoid future storage issues. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.t: Create an Amazon S3 File Gateway to extend the company's storage space. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the data to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 7 days.
o.w: An S3 File Gateway extends local storage capacity by presenting an SMB or NFS share backed by S3, preserving low-latency local access to new files, while an S3 Lifecycle rule automatically archives files older than 7 days to Glacier Deep Archive, satisfying the lifecycle management requirement at minimal cost.

o.t: Install a utility on each user's computer to access Amazon S3. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the data to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 7 days.
o.w: Requiring every user's computer to install a utility and access S3 directly abandons the existing SMB file-sharing workflow, creating disruption and more operational effort than a transparent gateway, and Glacier Flexible Retrieval costs more than Deep Archive for files that are rarely accessed.

o.t: Use AWS DataSync to copy data that is older than 7 days from the SMB file server to AWS.
o.w: DataSync only performs scheduled or one-time copy jobs; it does not provide an ongoing low-latency file share for users nor does it itself manage automatic storage-class lifecycle transitions, so it does not fully meet the requirement.

o.t: Create an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system to extend the company's storage space.
o.w: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server adds capacity but on its own does not include S3-based lifecycle management to automatically archive old data to a low-cost archive tier, since that capability belongs to S3 Lifecycle policies, not FSx.

explain: Option B: Amazon S3 File Gateway provides a hybrid cloud storage solution, integrating on-premises environments with cloud storage. Files written to the file share are automatically saved as S3 objects. With S3 Lifecycle policies, you can transition objects between storage classes. Transitioning to Glacier Deep Archive is suitable for rarely accessed files. This solution addresses both the storage capacity and lifecycle management requirements.

q: A company uses AWS and sells access to copyrighted images. The company’s global customer base needs to be able to access these images quickly. The company must deny access to users from specific countries. The company wants to minimize costs as much as possible. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.t: Use Amazon S3 to store the images. Turn on multi-factor authentication (MFA) and public bucket access. Provide customers with a link to the S3 bucket.
o.w: Making the bucket public and turning on MFA (which only protects object deletion) defeats the purpose of restricting access to paying customers and provides no mechanism to block specific countries.

o.t: Use Amazon EC2 instances that are behind Application Load Balancers (ALBs) to store the images. Deploy the instances only in the countries the company services. Provide customers with links to the ALBs for their specific country's instances.
o.w: Deploying and maintaining separate EC2 and ALB infrastructure in every served country is far more expensive and operationally heavy than using a single global CDN with built-in geographic restriction.

o.t: Use Amazon S3 to store the images. Create an IAM user for each customer. Add the users to a group that has permission to access the S3 bucket.
o.w: Creating and managing an individual IAM user for every customer does not scale well, adds significant administrative overhead, and IAM policies are not designed to enforce country-based access restrictions.

o.t: Use Amazon S3 to store the images. Use Amazon CloudFront to distribute the images with geographic restrictions. Provide a signed URL for each customer to access the data in CloudFront.
o.w: CloudFront can cache images globally at edge locations for fast access while its built-in geographic restriction feature blocks specific countries, and signed URLs restrict access to only paying customers, all at CloudFront's standard, usage-based cost with no extra infrastructure.

explain:
By using CloudFront, you can cache and serve the images from edge locations around the world, improving access speed for global customers.
Geographic Restrictions in CloudFront: CloudFront allows you to set up geographic restrictions to deny access to users from specific countries.

q: A company needs to minimize the cost of its 1 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection. The company's average connection utilization is less than 10%. A solutions architect must recommend a solution that will reduce the cost without compromising security. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.t: Set up a new 1 Gbps Direct Connect connection. Share the connection with another AWS account.
o.w: Setting up another full 1 Gbps dedicated connection does not reduce the cost of the existing underutilized capacity; sharing it with another account does not shrink the bandwidth or bill for the company's own usage.

o.t: Contact an AWS Direct Connect Partner to order a 200 Mbps hosted connection for an existing AWS account.
o.w: A hosted connection ordered through an AWS Direct Connect Partner can be provisioned at exactly the smaller bandwidth needed, such as 200 Mbps, reducing the monthly cost to match actual utilization while keeping the same private, secure connectivity.

o.t: Set up a new 200 Mbps Direct Connect connection in the AWS Management Console.
o.w: Dedicated Direct Connect connections provisioned directly in the AWS console are only available starting at 1 Gbps; sub-1-Gbps speeds require a hosted connection ordered through a Direct Connect Partner, so this option is not available as described.

o.t: Contact an AWS Direct Connect Partner to order a 1 Gbps connection. Share the connection with another AWS account.
o.w: Ordering a full 1 Gbps hosted connection and sharing it does not reduce the capacity, and therefore the cost, below what is already provisioned; the company needs a smaller hosted connection, not a shared full-size one.

q: A company is storing backup files by using Amazon S3 Standard storage. The files are accessed frequently for 1 month. However, the files are not accessed after 1 month. The company must keep the files indefinitely. Which storage solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.t: Configure S3 Intelligent-Tiering to automatically migrate objects.
o.w: S3 Intelligent-Tiering's automatic tiers carry a small monthly per-object monitoring fee, and even its deepest default archive tiers do not match Glacier Deep Archive's price floor for data that will never be accessed again after the first month.

o.t: Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration to transition objects from S3 Standard to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 1 month.
o.w: S3 Standard-IA is more expensive per GB than Glacier Deep Archive, and since the files are never accessed again after the first month, there is no benefit from IA's faster retrieval time that would justify its higher storage cost for indefinite retention.

o.t: Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration to transition objects from S3 Standard to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) after 1 month.
o.w: S3 One Zone-IA stores data in a single Availability Zone, reducing durability and resilience, and it is still priced higher than Glacier Deep Archive for data kept indefinitely and never read again, so it is not the most cost-effective choice.

o.t: Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration to transition objects from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 month.
o.w: S3 Glacier Deep Archive is AWS's lowest-cost storage class, ideal for backup data that must be retained indefinitely but is never accessed after the first month, and an S3 Lifecycle rule automates the transition after the 1-month frequent-access window.

explain:
Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive is a secure, durable, and extremely low-cost Amazon S3 storage class for long-term retention of data that is rarely accessed and for which retrieval times of several hours are acceptable. It is the lowest-cost storage option in Amazon S3, making it a cost-effective choice for storing backup files that are not accessed after 1 month.

You can use an S3 Lifecycle configuration to automatically transition objects from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 month. This will minimize the storage costs for the backup files that are not accessed frequently.

q: A company is migrating its workloads to AWS. The company has transactional and sensitive data in its databases. The company wants to use AWS Cloud solutions to increase security and reduce operational overhead for the databases. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.t: Migrate the data to Amazon S3 Use Amazon Macie for data security and protection
o.w: Amazon Macie discovers and classifies sensitive data but does not provide the transactional database engine the company needs to run its relational workloads, so migrating structured transactional data to S3 is not an appropriate substitute for a database.

o.t: Migrate the databases to Amazon RDS Configure encryption at rest.
o.w: Amazon RDS is a managed relational database that removes operational burdens like patching, backups, and provisioning, and enabling encryption at rest adds strong security for sensitive data with just a configuration setting.

o.t: Migrate the databases to Amazon EC2. Use an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) AWS managed key for encryption.
o.w: Running the database on self-managed EC2 instances means the company still has to manage the operating system, database engine patches, backups, and high availability itself, which is the opposite of reducing operational overhead compared to a managed RDS instance.

o.t: Migrate the database to Amazon RDS. Use Amazon CloudWatch Logs for data security and protection.
o.w: CloudWatch Logs is a logging and monitoring service; it does not encrypt or otherwise protect data at rest, so it does not address the data security requirement at all.

explain:
Amazon RDS (Relational Database Service) is a fully managed database service that simplifies database management tasks, such as hardware provisioning, patching, and backups.

Encryption at Rest
Amazon RDS supports encryption at rest, which means data stored in the database is automatically encrypted. This provides an additional layer of security for sensitive data.
Managed Service:
Amazon RDS is a managed service, meaning AWS takes care of operational aspects such as hardware maintenance, software patching, and backups. This reduces operational overhead for the company.

q: An application running on an Amazon EC2 instance in VPC-A needs to access files in another EC2 instance in VPC-B. Both VPCs are in separate AWS accounts. The network administrator needs to design a solution to configure secure access to EC2 instance in VPC-B from VPC-A. The connectivity should not have a single point of failure or bandwidth concerns. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.t: Set up VPC gateway endpoints for the EC2 instance running in VPC-B.
o.w: Gateway endpoints only provide private access to supported AWS services like S3 or DynamoDB; they cannot be used to connect an EC2 instance to another EC2 instance in a different VPC.

o.t: Create a private virtual interface (VIF) for the EC2 instance running in VPC-B and add appropriate routes from VPC-A.
o.w: A private virtual interface is a Direct Connect construct used to connect an on-premises network to a VPC over a dedicated line; it is not the mechanism for connecting two VPCs directly to each other.

o.t: Set up a VPC peering connection between VPC-A and VPC-B.
o.w: VPC peering establishes a direct, private network connection between the two VPCs using each instance's private IP addresses, with no intermediate gateway or single point of failure, and it is not limited by any additional bandwidth bottleneck beyond the instances' own network capacity.

o.t: Attach a virtual private gateway to VPC-B and set up routing from VPC-A.
o.w: A virtual private gateway is the VPC-side endpoint for a VPN or Direct Connect connection to an external network; it is not used to connect one VPC directly to another VPC.

explain: A VPC peering connection allows secure communication between instances in different VPCs using private IP addresses without the need for internet gateways, VPN connections, or NAT devices. By setting it up, the application running in VPC-A can directly access the EC2 in VPC-B without going through the public internet or any single point of failure.

q: A solutions architect is designing a multi-tier application for a company. The application's users upload images from a mobile device. The application generates a thumbnail of each image and returns a message to the user to confirm that the image was uploaded successfully. The thumbnail generation can take up to 60 seconds, but the company wants to provide a faster response time to its users to notify them that the original image was received. The solutions architect must design the application to asynchronously dispatch requests to the different application tiers. What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.t: Create an AWS Step Functions workflow. Configure Step Functions to handle the orchestration between the application tiers and alert the user when thumbnail generation is complete.
o.w: Step Functions orchestrates a workflow and would still tie the user-facing response to tracking the state machine's progress toward thumbnail completion, rather than giving the fast, decoupled initial response the company wants.

o.t: Create Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification topics and subscriptions. Use one subscription with the application to generate the thumbnail after the image upload is complete. Use a second subscription to message the user's mobile app by way of a push notification after thumbnail generation is complete.
o.w: SNS is a push-based pub/sub service without the message persistence and retry semantics a worker process needs to pull jobs at its own pace; it is not designed to hold a backlog of thumbnail-generation jobs the way a queue is.

o.t: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) message queue. As images are uploaded, place a message on the SQS queue for thumbnail generation. Alert the user through an application message that the image was received.
o.w: Placing a message on an SQS queue immediately after upload lets the application return a received confirmation to the user right away, while a separate worker processes the queue asynchronously to generate thumbnails whenever it can, directly matching the decoupled, fast-response requirement.

o.t: Write a custom AWS Lambda function to generate the thumbnail and alert the user. Use the image upload process as an event source to invoke the Lambda function.
o.w: Invoking a Lambda function synchronously tied to the upload event to both generate the thumbnail and alert the user still ties the user-facing response to the time-consuming thumbnail generation step unless significant additional asynchronous plumbing is added.

explain: Amazon SQS (Simple Queue Service): SQS is a fully managed message queuing service that enables decoupling of the components of a cloud application. By creating an SQS message queue, the image upload process can place messages in the queue for thumbnail generation.

q: A company is expecting rapid growth in the near future. A solutions architect needs to configure existing users and grant permissions to new users on AWS. The solutions architect has decided to create IAM groups. The solutions architect will add the new users to IAM groups based on department. Which additional action is the MOST secure way to grant permissions to the new users?

o.t: Create IAM roles that have least privilege permission. Attach the roles to the IAM groups
o.w: IAM roles cannot be attached to IAM groups; roles are assumed by users, applications, or services, not inherited through group membership, so this is not a valid IAM construct.

o.t: Create an IAM policy that grants least privilege permission. Attach the policy to the IAM groups
o.w: Attaching a least-privilege IAM policy directly to the IAM groups ensures every user added to a group automatically inherits exactly the permissions needed for their department, which is the standard, secure way to manage permissions at scale through groups.

o.t: Apply service control policies (SCPs) to manage access permissions
o.w: Service control policies apply at the AWS Organizations level to set permission guardrails across accounts or organizational units; they do not grant permissions to individual users and are not the mechanism for day-to-day access within a single account.

o.t: Create IAM roles. Associate the roles with a permissions boundary that defines the maximum permissions
o.w: Like IAM roles, permissions boundaries apply to roles or users directly rather than being attached to or associated with IAM groups, making this an invalid way to grant group-based permissions.

explain: Creating an IAM policy that grants the least privilege required for the users' tasks is a security best practice. By attaching this policy to IAM groups, you ensure that new users added to these groups inherit the specific permissions defined in the policy.

q: A company must migrate 20 TB of data from a data center to the AWS Cloud within 30 days. The company’s network bandwidth is limited to 15 Mbps and cannot exceed 70% utilization. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.t: Use AWS DataSync.
o.w: At 15 Mbps with a 70 percent utilization cap, transferring 20 TB online, even with an efficient transfer tool, would take far longer than 30 days, since the fundamental constraint is the network link itself rather than the transfer tool used.

o.t: Use AWS Snowball.
o.w: AWS Snowball physically ships a storage device to transfer the 20 TB offline, bypassing the limited 15 Mbps network link entirely and reliably completing the migration within the 30-day window.

o.t: Use a secure VPN connection.
o.w: Adding a VPN over the same constrained 15 Mbps link does not increase available bandwidth; the same network bottleneck still makes transferring 20 TB within 30 days infeasible.

o.t: Use Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration.
o.w: S3 Transfer Acceleration speeds up transfers by routing through CloudFront edge locations, but it cannot exceed the bandwidth ceiling of the company's actual 15 Mbps internet connection, so it does not solve the fundamental bandwidth constraint.

explain: AWS Snowball is a physical data transport solution that helps customers transfer large amounts of data into and out of AWS. It addresses challenges associated with large-scale data transfers, particularly when network constraints, transfer times, or security concerns make online data transfer less practical.

q: A company is launching a new application deployed on an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster and is using the Fargate launch type for ECS tasks. The company is monitoring CPU and memory usage because it is expecting high traffic to the application upon its launch. However, the company wants to reduce costs when utilization decreases. What should a solutions architect recommend?

o.t: Use an AWS Lambda function to scale Amazon ECS based on metric breaches that trigger an Amazon CloudWatch alarm.
o.w: Building a custom Lambda function to react to CloudWatch alarms and scale ECS reinvents functionality that AWS Application Auto Scaling already provides natively and more reliably, adding unnecessary custom code and operational burden.

o.t: Use AWS Application Auto Scaling with target tracking policies to scale when ECS metric breaches trigger an Amazon CloudWatch alarm.
o.w: AWS Application Auto Scaling integrates natively with ECS services running on Fargate and uses target tracking policies to automatically adjust the desired task count based on CPU or memory metrics, scaling down and reducing cost as utilization drops with no infrastructure to manage.

o.t: Use Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling to scale at certain periods based on previous traffic patterns.
o.w: Fargate tasks do not run on customer-managed EC2 instances, so Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling based on previous traffic patterns does not apply, since there are no EC2 instances in this architecture to scale.

o.t: Use Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling with simple scaling policies to scale when ECS metric breaches trigger an Amazon CloudWatch alarm.
o.w: The same fundamental mismatch applies: since the tasks use the Fargate launch type, there is no underlying EC2 Auto Scaling group to attach a scaling policy to.

explain:
AWS Application Auto Scaling is a service that can automatically adjust the number of running ECS tasks or services based on specified CloudWatch metrics.
Target tracking policies allow you to set a target value for a specific metric, and AWS Application Auto Scaling automatically adjusts the desired task count to maintain the target.
By using target tracking policies, you can ensure that the ECS cluster scales up or down based on the application's demand while maintaining a balance between cost efficiency and performance.

q: A company uses NFS to store large video files in on-premises network attached storage. Each video file ranges in size from 1 MB to 500 GB. The total storage is 70 TB and is no longer growing. The company decides to migrate the video files to Amazon S3. The company must migrate the video files as soon as possible while using the least possible network bandwidth. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.t: Create an AWS Snowball Edge job. Receive a Snowball Edge device on premises. Use the Snowball Edge client to transfer data to the device. Return the device so that AWS can import the data into Amazon S3.
o.w: An AWS Snowball Edge device lets the company copy all 70 TB locally at high speed onto the device and ship it to AWS for import into S3, using essentially no network bandwidth for the bulk transfer.

o.t: Deploy an S3 File Gateway on premises. Create a public service endpoint to connect to the S3 File Gateway. Create an S3 bucket. Create a new NFS file share on the S3 File Gateway. Point the new file share to the S3 bucket. Transfer the data from the existing NFS file share to the S3 File Gateway.
o.w: An S3 File Gateway still transfers all data over the network connection to S3 as it is written, consuming significant internet bandwidth for the full 70 TB rather than minimizing it.

o.t: Set up an AWS Direct Connect connection between the on-premises network and AWS. Deploy an S3 File Gateway on premises. Create a public virtual interface (VIF) to connect to the S3 File Gateway. Create an S3 bucket. Create a new NFS file share on the S3 File Gateway. Point the new file share to the S3 bucket. Transfer the data from the existing NFS file share to the S3 File Gateway.
o.w: Setting up a dedicated Direct Connect connection just for this one-time 70 TB migration is a large, time-consuming, and costly undertaking, and the transfer would still consume network bandwidth, now over the Direct Connect link, rather than avoiding it.

o.t: Create an S3 bucket. Create an IAM role that has permissions to write to the S3 bucket. Use the AWS CLI to copy all files locally to the S3 bucket.
o.w: Copying 70 TB directly over the internet with the CLI uses the full amount of available network bandwidth for an extended period, which does not minimize bandwidth usage the way an offline device transfer does.

explain: On a Snowball Edge device you can copy files with a speed of up to 100Gbps. 70TB will take around 5600 seconds, so very quickly, less than 2 hours. The downside is that it'll take between 4-6 working days to receive the device and then another 2-3 working days to send it back and for AWS to move the data onto S3 once it reaches them. Total time: 6-9 working days. Bandwidth used: 0.

q: A company runs its application on an Oracle database. The company plans to quickly migrate to AWS because of limited resources for the database, backup administration, and data center maintenance. The application uses third-party database features that require privileged access. Which solution will help the company migrate the database to AWS MOST cost-effectively?

o.t: Migrate the database to Amazon RDS Custom for Oracle. Customize the database settings to support third-party features.
o.w: Amazon RDS Custom for Oracle provides the managed-service benefits of RDS, such as automated backups and patching assistance, while still granting the OS- and database-level privileged access that the third-party features require, avoiding a costly full application or database rewrite.

o.t: Migrate the database to Amazon RDS for Oracle. Replace third-party features with cloud services.
o.w: Standard RDS for Oracle does not grant the privileged access many third-party extensions need, and replacing those features outright could require significant re-engineering effort and ongoing cost, working against a quick, cost-effective migration.

o.t: Migrate the database to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL by rewriting the application code to remove dependency on Oracle APEX.
o.w: Rewriting the application to remove Oracle-specific dependencies and move to PostgreSQL is a large, time-consuming migration project, contradicting the company's goal of quickly migrating given its limited resources.

o.t: Migrate the database to an Amazon EC2 Amazon Machine Image (AMI) for Oracle. Customize the database settings to support third-party features.
o.w: Running Oracle on a self-managed EC2 AMI gives full privileged access but makes the company responsible again for all backup, patching, and maintenance, exactly the operational burden it is trying to escape by moving to AWS, making it less cost-effective than a managed option.

q: A company is migrating a distributed application to AWS. The application serves variable workloads. The legacy platform consists of a primary server that coordinates jobs across multiple compute nodes. The company wants to modernize the application with a solution that maximizes resiliency and scalability. How should a solutions architect design the architecture to meet these requirements?

o.t: Implement the primary server and the compute nodes with Amazon EC2 instances that are managed in an Auto Scaling group. Configure AWS CloudTrail as a destination for the jobs. Configure EC2 Auto Scaling based on the load on the primary server.
o.w: Keeping a single primary server as a coordinator reintroduces a single point of failure, and CloudTrail records API activity rather than application job data, so it is not a valid destination for the jobs, making this design both less resilient and technically invalid.

o.t: Configure an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue as a destination for the jobs. Implement the compute nodes with Amazon EC2 instances that are managed in an Auto Scaling group. Configure EC2 Auto Scaling based on the size of the queue.
o.w: Routing jobs through an SQS queue removes the single coordinating server as a bottleneck and single point of failure, and scaling the compute node Auto Scaling group based on queue depth directly ties capacity to actual workload, maximizing both resiliency and scalability.

o.t: Configure an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue as a destination for the jobs. Implement the compute nodes with Amazon EC2 instances that are managed in an Auto Scaling group. Configure EC2 Auto Scaling to use scheduled scaling.
o.w: Scheduled scaling adjusts capacity on a fixed time-based schedule rather than reacting to the actual, variable size of the workload, so it does not scale appropriately for unpredictable job volume the way scaling on queue depth does.

o.t: Implement the primary server and the compute nodes with Amazon EC2 instances that are managed in an Auto Scaling group. Configure Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) as a destination for the jobs. Configure EC2 Auto Scaling based on the load on the compute nodes.
o.w: Retaining a single primary coordinator server is still a single point of failure, and EventBridge is an event bus for routing events between services rather than a durable job queue designed to buffer and distribute work items to compute nodes.

explain: Option B: This option provides a decoupled architecture where the jobs are sent to an SQS queue. The compute nodes (EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group) can then process these jobs. Scaling based on the size of the SQS queue (the number of messages) allows the architecture to adapt to variable workloads, scaling out when the queue depth increases and scaling in when the depth decreases.

q: A company is hosting a web application from an Amazon S3 bucket. The application uses Amazon Cognito as an identity provider to authenticate users and return a JSON Web Token (JWT) that provides access to protected resources that are stored in another S3 bucket. Upon deployment of the application, users report errors and are unable to access the protected content. A solutions architect must resolve this issue by providing proper permissions so that users can access the protected content. Which solution meets these requirements?

o.t: Update the Amazon Cognito pool to use custom attribute mappings within the identity pool and grant users the proper permissions to access the protected content.
o.w: Custom attribute mappings on a Cognito user pool manage user profile data, not the AWS permissions granted after authentication, so they do not control access to S3 resources.

o.t: Update the S3 ACL to allow the application to access the protected content.
o.w: S3 ACLs control object or bucket-level access grants directly, but the application is using Cognito-issued temporary credentials through an identity pool role, so the access problem lies in that role's permissions, not the bucket ACL.

o.t: Redeploy the application to Amazon S3 to prevent eventually consistent reads in the S3 bucket from affecting the ability of users to access the protected content.
o.w: S3 provides strong read-after-write consistency for new objects, so this is not an eventual-consistency issue at all, and redeploying the application would not change the underlying IAM permissions problem causing the access errors.

o.t: Update the Amazon Cognito identity pool to assume the proper IAM role for access to the protected content.
o.w: A Cognito identity pool maps authenticated users to an IAM role with temporary credentials, so updating that role to include the necessary S3 permissions, such as s3:GetObject, is what actually grants users access to the protected content.

explain:
Amazon Cognito Identity Pool: When users authenticate through Amazon Cognito, they assume roles that determine their access to AWS resources. By updating the Cognito identity pool, you can configure it to assume the proper IAM role that has the necessary permissions to access the protected content stored in the S3 bucket.

IAM Role Permissions: The IAM role associated with the identity pool should have the required permissions (e.g., S3 getObject permissions) to access the protected content in the S3 bucket.

q: A company is building an ecommerce application and needs to store sensitive customer information. The company needs to give customers the ability to complete purchase transactions on the website. The company also needs to ensure that sensitive customer data is protected, even from database administrators. Which solution meets these requirements?

o.t: Store sensitive data in an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Use EBS encryption to encrypt the data. Use an IAM instance role to restrict access.
o.w: EBS encryption protects data at the storage volume level, but a database administrator with access to the running database engine can still query and read the plaintext data through normal database access, so it does not hide data from DB admins.

o.t: Store sensitive data in Amazon S3. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) server-side encryption to encrypt the data. Use S3 bucket policies to restrict access.
o.w: S3 is not well suited to supporting transactional purchase operations the way a relational database is, and server-side encryption still decrypts data transparently for anyone with appropriate S3 read permissions, including administrators, so it does not protect data from privileged admins.

o.t: Store sensitive data in Amazon FSx for Windows Server. Mount the file share on application servers. Use Windows file permissions to restrict access.
o.w: Windows file permissions control OS-level file access but do not provide the transactional database capabilities needed for purchases, and anyone with sufficient file or share access, including admins, could still read the underlying files.

o.t: Store sensitive data in Amazon RDS for MySQL. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) client-side encryption to encrypt the data.
o.w: Client-side encryption with AWS KMS means the application encrypts sensitive data before it is ever sent to or stored in the RDS MySQL database, so even a database administrator with full access to the database can only see ciphertext, while the database still supports the transactional purchase workflow.

explain:
Amazon RDS (Relational Database Service) for MySQL is a managed relational database service that makes it easy to set up, operate, and scale a MySQL database in the cloud.
AWS Key Management Service (KMS) provides a way to create and control encryption keys. In the context of client-side encryption, the application (in this case, the ecommerce application) handles the encryption and decryption of data before it is stored in or retrieved from the database.

q: A company wants to improve its ability to clone large amounts of production data into a test environment in the same AWS Region. The data is stored in Amazon EC2 instances on Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. Modifications to the cloned data must not affect the production environment. The software that accesses this data requires consistently high I/O performance. A solutions architect needs to minimize the time that is required to clone the production data into the test environment. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.t: Configure the production EBS volumes to use the EBS Multi-Attach feature. Take EBS snapshots of the production EBS volumes. Attach the production EBS volumes to the EC2 instances in the test environment.
o.w: Using Multi-Attach to attach the actual production volumes to test instances means any writes from the test environment would modify the same underlying volume, directly risking production data rather than creating an isolated clone.

o.t: Take EBS snapshots of the production EBS volumes. Turn on the EBS fast snapshot restore feature on the EBS snapshots. Restore the snapshots into new EBS volumes. Attach the new EBS volumes to EC2 instances in the test environment.
o.w: Taking a snapshot and enabling fast snapshot restore lets new EBS volumes created from that snapshot be fully initialized immediately, delivering full provisioned IOPS performance right away, minimizing clone time while keeping the clone entirely separate from production.

o.t: Take EBS snapshots of the production EBS volumes. Restore the snapshots onto EC2 instance store volumes in the test environment.
o.w: Instance store volumes are ephemeral, non-persistent local storage tied to the instance's lifecycle; they are not a valid or durable restore target for EBS snapshots meant to support an ongoing high-IOPS workload in a test environment.

o.t: Take EBS snapshots of the production EBS volumes. Create and initialize new EBS volumes. Attach the new EBS volumes to EC2 instances in the test environment before restoring the volumes from the production EBS snapshots.
o.w: Attaching new EBS volumes to test instances before actually restoring the snapshot data onto them does not make procedural sense, and without fast snapshot restore, volumes restored from a snapshot still suffer lazy-loading latency on first access, slowing down the clone's usable performance.

explain: Amazon EBS fast snapshot restore (FSR) enables you to create a volume from a snapshot that is fully initialized at creation. This eliminates the latency of I/O operations on a block when it is accessed for the first time. Volumes that are created using fast snapshot restore instantly deliver all of their provisioned performance

q: A social media company is building a feature for its website. The feature will give users the ability to upload photos. The company expects significant increases in demand during large events and must ensure that the website can handle the upload traffic from users. Which solution meets these requirements with the MOST scalability?

o.t: Upload files from the user's browser to the application servers. Transfer the files to an Amazon S3 bucket.
o.w: Routing every photo upload through the application servers before forwarding to S3 makes the app tier the bottleneck during traffic surges, requiring it to scale, and incur compute cost, in lockstep with upload volume.

o.t: Provision an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Upload files directly from the user's browser to the file system.
o.w: Amazon EFS is a network file system intended for access from compute instances over NFS within a VPC; it is not designed to accept direct uploads from a user's web browser over the internet.

o.t: Provision an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway. Upload files directly from the user's browser to the file gateway.
o.w: An AWS Storage Gateway file gateway is meant to connect on-premises or VM-based applications to S3 via NFS or SMB; it is not designed to receive direct browser uploads over the internet from end users.

o.t: Generate Amazon S3 presigned URLs in the application. Upload files directly from the user's browser into an S3 bucket.
o.w: Generating S3 presigned URLs lets each user's browser upload directly to S3, bypassing the application servers entirely for the actual file transfer, which scales automatically with S3's massive built-in capacity regardless of upload spikes.

explain: Amazon S3 Presigned URLs: This approach allows the client (user's browser) to directly upload files to Amazon S3 using a presigned URL generated by the server. This offloads the file transfer process from the application servers and enables a direct upload to S3 from the client side.

q: A solutions architect is designing a workload that will store hourly energy consumption by business tenants in a building. The sensors will feed a database through HTTP requests that will add up usage for each tenant. The solutions architect must use managed services when possible. The workload will receive more features in the future as the solutions architect adds independent components. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.t: Use an Elastic Load Balancer that is supported by an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances to receive and process the data from the sensors. Use an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) shared file system to store the processed data.
o.w: Running an Elastic Load Balancer in front of a self-managed EC2 Auto Scaling group means the company still has to patch, scale, and operate servers itself, which is more operational overhead than fully managed services.

o.t: Use Amazon API Gateway with AWS Lambda functions to receive the data from the sensors, process the data, and store the data in a Microsoft SQL Server Express database on an Amazon EC2 instance.
o.w: Running a SQL Server Express database on a self-managed EC2 instance reintroduces server management, patching, and scaling responsibilities, and SQL Server Express also has capacity limitations unsuitable for a growing workload, where a managed database service would avoid both issues.

o.t: Use an Elastic Load Balancer that is supported by an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances to receive and process the data from the sensors. Use an Amazon S3 bucket to store the processed data.
o.w: The compute tier still carries the same server-management overhead as running EC2 behind an ELB, and S3 is object storage rather than a structured database well suited for storing and incrementally updating per-tenant usage totals.

o.t: Use Amazon API Gateway with AWS Lambda functions to receive the data from the sensors, process the data, and store the data in an Amazon DynamoDB table.
o.w: API Gateway and Lambda are both fully managed and scale automatically with incoming sensor requests, and DynamoDB is a fully managed NoSQL database well suited to storing and updating per-tenant usage totals, together requiring no server management and allowing independent components to be added later with minimal coupling.

explain:
Amazon API Gateway is a fully managed service that makes it easy for developers to create, publish, maintain, monitor, and secure APIs at any scale. It acts as an entry point for HTTP requests and can handle the communication with the sensors.
In this scenario, you can use Lambda functions to process the data received from the sensors. 
Amazon DynamoDB is a fully managed NoSQL database that can handle the storage of the hourly energy consumption data.

q: A company has an application that is backed by an Amazon DynamoDB table. The company’s compliance requirements specify that database backups must be taken every month, must be available for 6 months, and must be retained for 7 years. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.t: Use the AWS CLI to create an on-demand backup of the DynamoDB table. Set up an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs the command on the first day of each month with a cron expression. Specify in the command to transition the backups to cold storage after 6 months and to delete the backups after 7 years.
o.w: This approach requires custom scripting around the backup commands, and there is no native CLI option to specify a transition-to-cold-storage or multi-year deletion policy as part of an on-demand backup command, so those lifecycle behaviors would have to be built and maintained separately.

o.t: Create an AWS Backup plan to back up the DynamoDB table on the first day of each month. Specify a lifecycle policy that transitions the backup to cold storage after 6 months. Set the retention period for each backup to 7 years.
o.w: AWS Backup natively schedules recurring DynamoDB backups through a backup plan and supports lifecycle rules that transition backups to cold storage after a set period and expire them after a defined retention period, covering the entire monthly, 6-month, and 7-year requirement with no custom scripting.

o.t: Create a DynamoDB on-demand backup of the DynamoDB table on the first day of each month. Transition the backup to Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 6 months. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to delete backups that are older than 7 years.
o.w: DynamoDB on-demand backups are stored within the DynamoDB backup service rather than as objects in an S3 bucket, so an S3 Lifecycle policy cannot be applied to transition or delete them, mixing two separate storage systems incorrectly.

o.t: Use the AWS SDK to develop a script that creates an on-demand backup of the DynamoDB table. Set up an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs the script on the first day of each month. Create a second script that will run on the second day of each month to transition DynamoDB backups that are older than 6 months to cold storage and to delete backups that are older than 7 years.
o.w: Writing and scheduling two separate custom scripts to create backups and manage their lifecycle duplicates functionality AWS Backup already provides natively, adding unnecessary custom code to build, test, and maintain.

explain:
AWS Backup will automatically take full backups of the DynamoDB table on the schedule defined in the backup plan (the first of each month).
The lifecycle policy can transition backups to cold storage after 6 months, meeting that requirement.
Setting a 7-year retention period in the backup plan will ensure each backup is retained for 7 years as required.
AWS Backup manages the backup jobs and lifecycle policies, requiring no custom scripting or management.
